the-sculpture-and-mural-decorations-of-t: Stella Perry's pictorial survey records the art of the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition in San Francisco — the sculptures and murals that adorned its palaces and courts. Photographs and descriptions preserve works many visitors saw only once. For lovers of public art, the book is a treasured record of a fair that celebrated the city's rebirth after the 1906 earthquake.
the-siksha-patri-of-the-svami-narayana-s: Sir Monier Monier-Williams translates the Siksha-Patri, the code of the Swami-Narayana sect — its rules for holy living. This pioneering rendering opened a Hindu reform movement to English study. A landmark of religious scholarship. Precepts for daily holiness shine through this careful translation.
the-resources-of-quinola-a-comedy-in-a-p: Balzac's Resources of Quinola — a comedy of a ruined inventor and his desperate schemes — shows the great novelist as playwright. His Parisian sharpness and eye for character enliven every scene. A lively curiosity from the master of the Human Comedy.
terre-napoleo-n-a-history-of-french-expl: Ernest Scott tells how French ships sought a Terre Napoléon in Australia — Baudin charting the south coast while Britain watched with fear. His fair-minded history gives French daring its due at last. A fine piece of righting old wrongs.
